title: Minimum Cost Walk in Weighted Graph
summary: Given an undirected weighted graph with n vertices labeled from 0 to n-1 , where each edge has a weight, and a set of queries specifying start and end vertices, determine the minimum cost of a walk between each pair of vertices.
statement: Given an undirected weighted graph with n vertices labeled from 0 to n-1 , where each edge has a weight, and a set of queries specifying start and end vertices, determine the minimum cost of a walk between each pair of vertices. The cost of a walk is defined as the bitwise AND of the weights of the edges traversed during the walk. If no such walk exists between a pair of vertices, return -1 for that query.
constraints: Vertices are 0 through n-1; edges are undirected and may repeat, with nonnegative weights.
A walk may repeat vertices and edges; its cost is the bitwise AND of every traversed edge weight.
For each query return zero for equal endpoints, -1 across components, or the minimum walk cost otherwise.
hints: Within one connected component a walk can detour over every edge before reaching its destination, and extra AND operands can only reduce cost.
Union all endpoints, AND every edge weight into its final component, then answer connectivity queries.
Build DSU; componentCost[root]&=weight for all edges; answer 0 for u=v, cost for same roots, else -1.
A traversal can include all component edges, achieving their AND, and no walk can clear a bit present in every component edge.
editorial: A traversal can include all component edges, achieving their AND, and no walk can clear a bit present in every component edge.

tests.explanation: Vertices zero and three share a component whose edge-weight AND is one; vertex four is disconnected.
A walk can include all component edges for AND zero, while an equal-endpoint query costs zero.
